greek: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ Ιακωβ εἶδεν καὶ ἰδοὺ Ησαυ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ ἐρχόμενος καὶ τετρακόσιοι ἄνδρες μετʼ αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐπιδιεῖλεν Ιακωβ τὰ παιδία ἐπὶ Λειαν καὶ Ραχηλ καὶ τὰς δύο παιδίσκας
hint: Jacob looked up and saw Esau his brother coming, and four hundred men with him. And Jacob divided the children between Leah and Rachel and the two slave-girls

notes.text: ἐπιδιαιρέω, *to divide anew*, which Middle Liddell gives that sense and the middle's *to distribute among themselves*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts αὐτός before the second καί, and ἐπί before Ραχηλ.

names.gloss: (Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")
(Ησαυ, from Hebrew ʿĒśāw, usually connected with śēʿār, "hair")
(Λεια, from Hebrew Lēʾâ, of uncertain meaning, perhaps "wild cow")

greek: καὶ ἐποίησεν τὰς δύο παιδίσκας καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτῶν ἐν πρώτοις καὶ Λειαν καὶ τὰ παιδία αὐτῆς ὀπίσω καὶ Ραχηλ καὶ Ιωσηφ ἐσχάτους.
hint: and he put the two slave-girls and their sons first, and Leah and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph last.

notes.text: ἐν takes the word beside it into the unit; πρῶτος is filed under πρότερος, as at 8:5.

hint: And he looked up and saw the women and the children and said: What are these to you? And he said: The children with which God had mercy on your servant.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is Sukkôt, Succoth, the booths; the Greek translates the name, and Rahlfs prints it with a capital.
[[flag]] Rahlfs takes ἑαυτῷ from the Cairo Geniza witness; Codex Alexandrinus reads αὐτῷ.

reading: And [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[lifts off|lifts off, carries off, takes away, removes from, leads away, sails and marches away and departs|ἀπαίρω]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Σκηνάς]]; and [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] to himself [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] [[buildings|buildings, houses, dwellings, households and domestic establishments, households and inmates of the house, houses and families|οἰκία]] and [[to the flocks and herds|to the flocks and herds, to the single beasts, to the beasts for riding|κτῆνος]] of him [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] [[covered places|covered places, tents, camps, dwelling-places, temples|σκηνή]]; [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of|διά + accusative]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[of the place|of the place, of the local circumstances, of the position, of the passage in a book, of the topic, of the common-place, of the occasion and opportunity|τόπος]] [[of that|of that, of the one there, of the more remote|ἐκεῖνος]] [[name:Σκηναί]].

names.gloss: (Σκηναί, "tents", the Greek of Hebrew Sukkôt, Succoth, the booths)

greek: καὶ ἦλθεν Ιακωβ εἰς Σαλημ πόλιν Σικιμων, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν γῇ Χανααν, ὅτε ἦλθεν ἐκ τῆς Μεσοποταμίας Συρίας, καὶ παρενέβαλεν κατὰ πρόσωπον τῆς πόλεως.
hint: And Jacob came to Salem, a city of the Shechemites, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Mesopotamia of Syria, and he encamped before the face of the city.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *šālēm ʿîr šĕkem*, *safe to the city of Shechem*; the Greek reads Salem as a place-name.

reading: and [[came|came, went, went back and returned, were going to and intended, came within a little of and were near|ἔρχομαι]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Σαλημ]] [[city|city, citadel, country, body of citizens, state|πόλις]] [[name:Σικιμων]], which is [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, ground|ἐν; γῆ]] [[name:Χανααν]], [[when|when, sometimes|ὅτε]] [[came|came, went, went back and returned, were going to and intended, came within a little of and were near|ἔρχομαι]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] the [[name:Μεσοποταμίας]] [[name:Συρίας]], and [[put in beside|put in beside, inserted, interpolated, interposed, insinuated, put in line with, fell into line and encamped|παρεμβάλλω]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] [[of the city|of the city, of the citadel, of the country, of the body of citizens, of the state|πόλις]].

names.gloss: (Σαλημ, from Hebrew Šālēm, which the Hebrew hears in šālôm, "peace", and which the Hebrew of this verse reads as šālēm, "safe")
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)
(Μεσοποταμία, Greek, "the land between the rivers", for Hebrew Paddan-ʾĂrām)
(Συρία, the Greek name of the land; the Hebrew here is Paddan-ʾĂrām)

greek: καὶ ἐκτήσατο τὴν μερίδα τοῦ ἀγροῦ, οὗ ἔστησεν ἐκεῖ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, παρὰ Εμμωρ πατρὸς Συχεμ ἑκατὸν ἀμνῶν
hint: And he bought the portion of the field where he had set up his tent, from Hamor father of Shechem, for a hundred lambs

notes.text: A hundred lambs, where the Hebrew has a hundred *qĕśîṭâ*, a weight of silver the Greek does not name.

reading: and [[procured for himself|procured for himself, got, gained, acquired, brought upon himself and incurred, procured for another|κτάομαι]] [[the part|the part, the portion, the share, the parcel, the contribution, the part and division and class|μερίς]] [[of the field|of the field, of the lands, of the farm, of the country|ἀγρός]] , where [[made to stand|made to stand, set, stopped and stayed and checked, set up and raised, established and instituted, appointed, weighed|ἵστημι]] [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] [[the covered place|the covered place, the tent, the camp, the dwelling-place, the temple|σκηνή]] of him, [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near|παρά + genitive]] [[name:Εμμωρ]] [[of father|of father, of grandfather|πατήρ]] [[name:Συχεμ]] hundred of lambs

names.gloss: (Συχεμ, from Hebrew Šĕkem, "shoulder", the man who bears the city's name)

greek: καὶ ἔστησεν ἐκεῖ θυσιαστήριον καὶ ἐπεκαλέσατο τὸν θεὸν Ισραηλ.
hint: and he set up an altar there and called upon the God of Israel.

notes.text: The middle of ἐπικαλέω, *to call upon*, as at 4:26 and 12:8.

reading: and [[made to stand|made to stand, set, stopped and stayed and checked, set up and raised, established and instituted, appointed, weighed|ἵστημι]] [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] an altar and [[called upon for himself|called upon for himself, invoked and appealed to, invited, called in as a helper or ally, called before him and summoned, challenged|ἐπικαλέω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[name:Ισραηλ]].

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")
